leads.claim: The U.S. Military recovered material of extraterrestrial origin near Roswell, New Mexico, in July 1947.
leads.why: The document acknowledges the existence of a widely reported claim regarding the recovery of extraterrestrial material, though it ultimately argues against its validity.
leads.claimant: Major Jesse Marcel and other military/civilian witnesses
leads.quote: It involved the recovery by the U.S. Military of material alleged to be of extraterrestrial origin.

leads.claim: A witness claimed to have seen alien bodies related to the Roswell incident.
leads.why: The text references a specific claim about the existence of bodies, even while dismissing it as part of a larger, debunked narrative.
leads.claimant: Anonymous witness cited in a letter
leads.quote: we secured another first-hand witness to the bodies.

leads.claim: Jesse Marcel, Jr. saw unusual material recovered from the Foster Ranch that his father brought home.
leads.why: The claim involves a specific witness who allegedly handled the material, though the author concludes it was mundane.
leads.quote: Jesse Marcel, Jr., got a good look at the unusual material.

doc_verdict: The document explicitly denies the existence of any extraterrestrial material or secret programs, characterizing all such claims as hoaxes or misidentifications of mundane objects like radar reflectors.
